Every Drop Has a Second Life.

Understanding household RO water wastage and exploring an IoT-based solution for recovery and reuse.

01 · The problem 01 / 09
Every day, household RO purifiers discharge litres of reject water directly into drains.

This water is often discarded even though it may be suitable for certain non-drinking household uses after quality assessment.

04 · Focusing on RO 04 / 09

Of these, how many households use RO purifiers?

55%Of total electronic purifiers are RO

JalCycle focuses specifically on RO purifiers because the RO filtration process discharges a reject-water stream. Other electronic purifier technologies, such as UV or UF, generally do not produce this RO reject-water stream.

Applying this national market-share proxy to Maharashtra's estimated 22.74 lakh electronic-purifier households gives:

12.51 Lakh
Estimated RO-purifier households in Maharashtra
10.11 Lakh Urban RO households
2.40 Lakh Rural RO households
Source: Technopak national purifier-market analysis · NFHS-5 Maharashtra, Table 4 · Census 2011 Maharashtra household baseline. The 55% is a national proxy, not a measured Maharashtra installed-base share; household counts are estimates.

Introducing JalCycle.

An IoT-based system to collect, monitor, store and transfer RO reject water for suitable reuse.

📡

Measure

Flow sensors measure reject water generated and reused.

🛢️

Collect

Storage tanks with level monitoring and overflow protection.

⚙️

Transfer

Automatic pumps and suitable reuse connections.

🎁

Incentivise

Rewards based on measured water delivered to registered reuse points.

Separate non-potable plumbing, backflow protection and water-quality assessment are essential.

JalCycle · The solution IoT-enabled RO reject-water collection
A simple, measurable system

Internet of Things (IoT) based JalCycle

Assessment and water conservation of reject-water discharge from household water purifiers using the Internet of Things (IoT).

1. Measure at the pipe

A flow sensor measures reject-water quantity. The ESP32 processes the readings and sends volume data over Wi-Fi.

2. Collect and monitor

A solenoid valve diverts water into a portable tank, while a level sensor tracks how full the tank is.

3. Easy-to-shift portable tank

A 20-litre can-style tank with wheels and a handle can be moved and emptied for suitable non-drinking household uses.

💧

Measure and monitor

The flow sensor measures the amount of RO reject water discharged, while the water-level sensor tracks the tank's remaining storage capacity. The ESP32 sends volume readings over Wi-Fi and alerts the household when the tank is full.

🛢️

Divert and collect

The solenoid valve directs reject water into a portable storage tank. The arrangement keeps the RO reject outlet unrestricted and avoids creating backpressure.

📊

Record and reuse

A mobile or web dashboard records the water collected and reused. Stored water is intended for suitable non-drinking household uses such as toilet flushing and floor cleaning.

821 CRORE LITRES

of freshwater can be saved every year in Maharashtra based households's water purifier alone.

It can be diverted to mopping/floor ceaning, utensil washing, toilet flushing. A single toilet flush leads to 3 litres of water discharge.

LOOK BEYOND TODAY'S ESTIMATE

What if we thought bigger?

This estimate uses the 2011 Census. Maharashtra's actual 2026 population and household water-purifier usage are likely to be much higher, so the real potential could be greater.

And why stop at households? The same IoT-based water-recovery approach could also be explored for air conditioners, corporates, hospitals, malls and other large establishments. Imagine the volume of water we could save if we extended this thinking everywhere.
